title: Costs and benefits of alternative food handling tactics help explain facultative exploitation of pollination mutualisms
decision_basis: Primary experiments compare handling tactics, foraging efficiency, primary-robbing frequency and nectar standing crop across bee–plant combinations; no independently measured floral or visitor–flower access-geometry predictor is fitted against robbery route use.
notes: Mechanistically relevant tactic-economy study, but outside the frozen direct access-geometry estimand.

title: Attraction of florivores and larcenists and interaction between antagonists in Senna rugosa (Fabaceae)
decision_basis: Flower size is analyzed as an attraction/display signal for florivores and larcenists rather than as legitimate-access geometry or visitor–flower mismatch predicting robbery route use.
notes: Floral display/antagonist-attraction study, not the frozen access-constraint relation.

title: Integrating morphological and molecular perspectives on foraging tactic constancy in a nectar-robbing bumble bee
decision_basis: Primary field study independently measures Bombus bifarius body size and classifies repeated legitimate, secondary-robbing and switching tactics on Linaria vulgaris; body size is quantitatively associated with tactic and the paper explicitly links size to ability to reach nectar through the legitimate floral opening.
notes: Eligibility frozen before direction coding; direction remains uncoded in this batch.

title: Asymmetrical disassortative pollination in a distylous primrose: the complementary roles of bumblebee nectar robbers and syrphid flies
decision_basis: Study compares floral morphs, pollinator assemblages and reproductive consequences of nectar-robbing bumblebees versus syrphid flies; it does not quantitatively model a measured access-geometry variable as the predictor of robbery route use.
notes: Heterostyly/pollination-efficiency study with robbers, but no direct geometry-to-robbery response model.

title: Cheaters among pollinators: Floral traits drive spatiotemporal variation in nectar robbing and thieving in Afrotropical rainforests
decision_basis: Preprint/version of the Sakhalkar et al. Afrotropical biological network already used as one of the two standardized Letter networks; it cannot add an independent formal direct-study denominator unit.
notes: Same biological program as published Ecosphere network 10.1002/ecs2.4696; retain only as bibliographic overlap.

title: Selective nectar robbing in a gynodioecious plant (Glechoma longituba) enhances female advantage
decision_basis: Primary study compares sex morphs and the reproductive consequences/pattern of selective nectar robbing; no independently measured access-geometry predictor is tested against robbery route probability or frequency.
notes: Sex-morph/reproductive-selection study rather than direct access geometry.

title: Foraging strategy predicts foraging economy in a facultative secondary nectar robber
decision_basis: Primary study tests foraging-strategy economics, primary-robbing frequency and nectar standing crop; route strategy predicts energetic efficiency rather than being modeled from an access-geometry variable.
notes: Frame DOI is a bibliographic issue-level identifier; primary article DOI is 10.1111/oik.04229. Predictor mismatch determines exclusion.

title: The Hidden Benefits of Pollinator Diversity for the Rangelands of the Great Plains: Western Prairie Fringed Orchids as a Case Study
decision_basis: Case study concerns pollinator diversity and orchid conservation; it does not estimate a route-resolved nectar-robbing outcome from access geometry.
notes: Same title also occurred in another bibliographic record already excluded; no direct robbery-route test.

title: Exploitation of Strobilanthes ixiocephala (Acanthaceae) flower buds by bees
decision_basis: Behavioral observations document bees piercing unopened buds to obtain pollen/nectar, but no quantitative variation in floral access geometry is tested against robbery/bypass probability or frequency.
notes: Natural-history evidence of bypass behavior without a geometry-response estimate.

title: Spatiotemporal Variations in Nectar Robbing and Its Effects on Reproduction in Salvia castanea Diels (Lamiaceae)
decision_basis: Primary analyses test spatiotemporal/population variation in nectar robbing and downstream reproductive effects; no access-geometry predictor is estimated against robbery route use.

title: Genetic variation, mating system, and nectar robbery in Aconitum lycoctonum (Ranunculaceae)
decision_basis: Doctoral thesis is an umbrella academic source containing component work, including the separately screened Oecologia floral-damage paper; it is not counted as an additional primary biological study program.
notes: Component primary paper(s) are screened separately, preventing double counting.
